experiments.description: Credit-risk portfolio experiment computing VaR, CVaR, EVaR (expectiles), and RVaR for a two-asset correlated default-loss model using canonical quantum amplitude estimation; performance is studied as the number of ancilla qubits m increases.

algorithm.variant: canonical QAE for risk measures; hybrid bisection search for expectiles; direct QAE for RVaR
algorithm.convergence_criteria: For expectiles: stop bisection when |y| < ϵ or |x2-x1|/2 < δ, or after N iterations. For QAE-based risk measures: repeated runs with varying m; no training convergence.

hyperparameters.gamma: approximately pi/4 for expectiles and RVaR; approximately pi/8 for VaR/CVaR (rule of thumb from later case study, not explicitly tied to this credit-risk figure)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Distribution of the total loss L is loaded into an n-qubit register; for the credit-risk example the standard normal latent factor Z is stored on 2 qubits, Bernoulli defaults X1 and X2 are loaded via controlled Ry rotations, and losses L1, L2 are computed by a sum circuit.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Risk measures of total loss L = L1 + ... + LK, with Lk = lambda_k X_k and correlated defaults p_k(z) = F((F^{-1}(p0_k) - sqrt(rho_k) z)/sqrt(1-rho_k)). Expectile uses h_X,alpha(x) = E[max{(1+beta)X - beta x, X}] and RVaR uses conditional expectation over a tail interval.
problem_formulation.num_ancilla_qubits: m for canonical QAE; comparator circuits also use additional ancillas, but the exact total is not fully enumerated in the paper

problem_instance.description: Two-asset credit portfolio with correlated defaults driven by a latent standard normal factor.

dataset_specification.latent_factor_distribution: standard normal truncated/discretized to [-2, 2] on 2 qubits
dataset_specification.preprocessing: Approximate default-probability rotation angles by first-order Taylor expansion around z=0; discretize Z on 4 points via affine map i -> 4/3 i - 2

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Load latent normal distribution with UZ; approximate Bernoulli default rotations using first-order expansion; compute total loss with sum circuit S; for expectiles, perform classical bisection over x using quantum-evaluated h_X,alpha.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: For canonical QAE, take the most frequent estimate over repeated runs; compare estimated risk measures to exact values.
implementation_details.notes: Figure 7 reports 1000 executions of QAE for the credit-risk example.

speedup_claims.conditions: via quantum amplitude estimation for risk-measure estimation
speedup_claims.caveats: Claim is inherited from the amplitude-estimation framework; the paper reports simulator/noisy-device experiments but does not benchmark wall-clock runtime against classical Monte Carlo.

scalability_data.metric_value: average result converges to exact value as m increases

experiments.description: Insurance claim-size experiment on a simulator: compute VaR, CVaR, EVaR, and RVaR for discretized lognormal and gamma claim-size distributions while varying the number of qubits used to load the distribution.

algorithm.variant: IQAE-based risk estimation on simulator; canonical QAE for expectile convergence plots
algorithm.convergence_criteria: IQAE target precision 0.05 and confidence level 0.01 for the qubit-scaling study; canonical QAE uses m ancilla qubits and the most frequent result.

hyperparameters.canonical_qae_ancilla_qubits_m: varied in plots; later noisy-device study fixes m=3

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Continuous density f is discretized on a bounded interval into 2^n points; the resulting probability mass function is loaded into an n-qubit register via state preparation. Risk measures are computed from the discretized random variable X.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Risk measures of -Y where Y is fitted by lognormal or gamma distributions; VaR/CVaR from quantiles and tail expectations; EVaR from expectiles; RVaR from conditional expectation over a quantile interval.
problem_formulation.num_ancilla_qubits: For canonical QAE, m ancilla qubits; comparator ancillas are used in the operator A but total count is not fully specified

problem_instance.description: Real insurance claim-size data from the Norwegian automobile dataset, fitted with lognormal and gamma distributions and then discretized for quantum loading.

preprocessing: fit parameters by method of moments
discretize the support on a bounded interval

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Fit lognormal and gamma distributions by method of moments; discretize the continuous density; load the discretized distribution into qubits; choose gamma scaling parameter gamma; for RVaR, estimate VaR endpoints and interval probability before computing the conditional expectation.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compare estimated risk measures against exact values; compute estimation error relative to interval length; average over repeated runs where applicable.

speedup_claims.caveats: No direct runtime comparison is reported; the paper studies estimation error versus qubit count on a simulator.

scalability_data.problem_size: number of qubits used to load the distribution
scalability_data.metric_value: error becomes sufficiently small (< 0.025 on the y-axis) as qubits increase

scalability_data.problem_size: number of qubits used to load the distribution
scalability_data.metric_value: good results when the number of qubits is sufficiently large

experiments.description: Noisy-simulator experiment emulating IBM Brisbane: compare canonical QAE, IQAE, and MLQAE for VaR, CVaR, EVaR, and RVaR on the discretized insurance distributions with limited qubits and varying shot counts.

algorithm.variant: canonical QAE vs iterative QAE vs maximum-likelihood QAE on noisy simulator
algorithm.convergence_criteria: IQAE uses confidence intervals with confidence level 0.05; MLQAE uses evaluation schedule 3; canonical QAE uses m=3 ancilla qubits.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same discretized distribution-loading setup as the simulator study, but restricted to 3 qubits for loading the distribution due to noise.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Same risk-measure objectives as in the simulator study; RVaR requires probability p in the denominator of the conditional expectation.
problem_formulation.num_ancilla_qubits: 3 ancilla qubits for canonical QAE; comparator ancillas for the operator A are present but not fully counted

problem_instance.description: Same insurance claim-size distributions as exp_2, evaluated under a noise model mimicking IBM Brisbane.

preprocessing: same fitted lognormal and gamma models as exp_2
restrict to 3 qubits for loading the distribution
vary number of shots to test robustness

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Use the same discretized distribution circuits as in the noiseless simulator study; run canonical QAE, IQAE, and MLQAE with the specified shot counts; for RVaR, compute VaR endpoints and interval probability before the conditional expectation.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Select the most frequent canonical-QAE outcome; compare estimation errors across methods and shot counts; report minimum estimation errors (e.g., 0.125 for IQAE/canonical QAE on gamma expectiles, 0.375 for MLQAE).

speedup_claims.conditions: amplitude-estimation-based risk estimation on noisy hardware/simulator
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper compares quantum variants against each other, not against a classical Monte Carlo runtime baseline.

scalability_data.metric_value: canonical QAE accuracy does not change with increased shots; IQAE/MLQAE can improve
expectile minimum estimation error 0.125 for IQAE and canonical QAE on gamma distribution
expectile minimum estimation error 0.375 for MLQAE on gamma distribution
